report.headline: Worth a closer look (55/100, high confidence): a lapsed Canon patent on driving liquid lenses by tuning the on/off timing of the voltage, in a real but small and mature niche.
report.what_it_is: This patent describes a lens made of two liquids that don't mix, sealed in a small container with electrodes, where applying voltage reshapes the boundary between the liquids and changes the focus. The key idea in the first claim is controlling focus by adjusting the duty ratio (the share of time the alternating voltage is on) rather than just the voltage level.

why_it_died.text: Canon paid the 4th- and 8th-year fees, then did not pay the 11.5-year fee, so the patent lapsed in October 2016 with about 5 years of term left. No reinstatement appears on record. The record does not say why Canon stopped paying. The score gives only modest weight to the idea that it died for money rather than merit (5.2 of 15).

case_for.point: Examiners kept treating this as important prior art. It was cited against 97 later applications and by 117 later filings overall, which is why it scores full marks on examiner relevance.
The underlying technology is in real products today. Corning sells Varioptic electrowetting lenses for industrial uses, marketed on low power, unlimited cycles and shock resistance.
Other companies kept building on it after it lapsed. Ten later filings by unrelated owners cite it with priority dates after 2016.
It was filed in only one jurisdiction, and the lapse appears to have left years of term unused, which is part of why it scores well on 'clear path'.

case_against.point: Momentum has stalled. No citing filings have priority dates from 2019 on, so recent momentum scored 0 of 20.
The market is small. Analysts put global liquid lens sales at roughly US$34-40M a year, growing about 5% a year. That is a tough base for a venture-scale business.
An established supplier already sells these lenses. A newcomer would compete with Corning Varioptic on a mature product.
Drive methods are still being patented by others. One example is a granted 2020s US patent on driving selected electrode sectors. Newer rights may sit right next to this idea.

blockers.point: There are 32 later patents by other owners that examiners cited against this one, and they may still be in force. They could cover improvements you would naturally want to use. This is worth checking with counsel.
The patent describes the concept, not how to make it. Expect to work out liquid choice, sealing and electrode processes yourself.
Some optics may fall under export controls (EAR Category 6). Products that include lasers must meet FDA CDRH laser standards.
If the lens goes into a wireless device, that product must meet many standards covered by other live patents and needs FCC authorization.

assumption_to_test.assumption: Industrial or camera-module buyers would switch from an established supplier like Corning Varioptic to a new liquid lens or driver offering, because duty-ratio control gives them a meaningful benefit such as lower cost, simpler electronics or better precision.
assumption_to_test.why_riskiest: The market is small and mature, with an incumbent already selling working products. If buyers see no reason to switch, the patent's technical idea does not become a business, however sound it is.
assumption_to_test.how_to_test: Buy one Varioptic evaluation lens and driver, or get a quote, and do a teardown to see how it is driven today (about $300-500). In parallel, run 10-15 customer interviews with machine-vision integrators and camera-module engineers. Ask what they pay, what frustrates them about current liquid lenses and drivers, and whether a cheaper or simpler driver would change their buying decision. Count how many would request a sample.

attorney_questions: Do any of the 32 later patents cited against this one, or newer drive-method patents such as US 11822095, appear to still be in force and to cover duty-ratio or similar AC drive control for electrowetting lenses?
Given the 2016 lapse for a missed 11.5-year fee and no reinstatement on record, is there any remaining risk tied to this patent or related Canon family members we should check?
Would our intended product (lens, driver, or camera module) raise export-control (EAR Category 6), FDA laser, or FCC issues we need to plan for?
report.disclaimer: Research and triage only, not legal advice. This report is not a patentability, validity or freedom-to-operate opinion. Patent status shown here comes from public records that can lag or be wrong. An expired patent is not the same as free to use: follow-on patents, regulatory exclusivity, trade secrets and standards can still block a product. Confirm with a registered patent attorney before acting.

signals.signal: The patent drew strong technical and examiner attention historically, which points to a foundational position in electrowetting variable-focus optics.

Citation momentum has faded. Some unrelated owners cited it after it lapsed, but no citing filings have priority dates from 2019 onward, so the patent itself is no longer a live reference point for new filings.

The underlying technology is commercially active. Electrowetting liquid lenses are sold today, and newer patents continue to refine electrode drive methods, which is the same problem area as this patent's AC duty-ratio control.
The addressable market looks niche. Analyst estimates put it in the tens of millions of dollars with modest single-digit growth, so a pure liquid-lens play may face limited headroom.

read.who_is_active: Corning, through its Varioptic line, is the named active commercial player selling electrowetting liquid lenses, and a separately granted patent (US 11822095) shows ongoing development of electrowetting drive methods by an owner not named in the evidence.
read.market_read: Electrowetting liquid lenses are a real but small market, served by at least one established supplier and seeing continued incremental innovation in drive electronics. A founder should treat this patent mainly as technical background in a mature niche, and should check the newer patent landscape around drive methods with qualified counsel before building on it.
